criterionInventory.rationale: Repository governance defines scoped change responsibility and review expectations; named human assignment remains pending.
The internal GRC control system establishes ownership, cadence, evidence, retention, and exception accountability.
No approved organizational structure and delegated-authority evidence is currently maintained in repository scope.
No approved competence, security training, or role-qualification evidence source is currently maintained.
The GRC control system requires accountable owners and time-bounded exceptions for assigned internal controls.
Repository documents do not yet establish an approved control for internal information quality and maintenance.
No approved evidence demonstrates internal distribution and acknowledgment of control responsibilities.
The service inventory alone does not evidence an approved process for external security and availability communications.
The linked GRC process and service inventory connect material risks to accountable controls, systems, and evidence.
Critical-journey accessibility verification is planned but lacks approved operating evidence and ownership.
The current risk register does not establish a separately approved fraud and abuse risk-assessment control.
The intended significant-change scope and evidence expectations require CPA confirmation before control mapping.
The GRC control system requires recurring evidence review and blocks approval when required evidence is missing or stale.
Time-bounded exception handling and owner review in the GRC process provide an internal deficiency-escalation mechanism.
The matrix schema defines explicit internal control activities, owners, cadence, evidence, retention, and exception timing.
The release-gate matrix defines the repository automation boundary and deterministic checks required before change promotion.
Repository governance documents scoped responsibilities and review constraints for internal control execution.
The identity and access boundary documents authenticated access rules and fail-closed authorization expectations.
No approved joiner, mover, leaver, and periodic logical-access inventory evidence is currently maintained.
Admin access controls require an authenticated administrator claim and reject unauthorized sensitive operations.
Physical-access responsibility and subservice-organization allocation require CPA confirmation for this boundary.
No approved periodic access-review and timely access-removal operating evidence is currently maintained.
Secret scanning exists by design, while web-header and DOM controls remain remediation work without approved cycles.
Secret-scanning design evidence exists, but its criterion alignment and operating scope require CPA confirmation.
No approved malware prevention, detection, and response control evidence is currently maintained in scope.
Dependency and vulnerability management is recorded as planned remediation without approved operating evidence.
Security monitoring and incident detection are planned within the incident-response control but are not operating.
Event evaluation and incident triage are planned within the incident-response control but are not operating.
Incident containment and recovery workflow is planned and currently represented only by a documented gap.
Post-incident remediation and control improvement are planned without approved operating evidence.
Admin change-control documentation and the release-gate matrix define scoped repository change authorization and checks.
The GRC control system connects business and technology risks to controls, owners, evidence, and exceptions.
Vendor governance is planned but has no approved owner, vendor inventory, review artifacts, or operating cycle.
Web performance objectives and regression checks are planned but lack approved targets and operating evidence.
Incident and recovery planning is recorded as a gap and lacks approved capacity and recovery operating evidence.
Backup and restore verification is planned but has no approved restore-test manifest or reviewed operating cycle.
